query: Identify a processing route and property optimization strategy for a lightweight, multi-principal element alloy system. The goal is to achieve high density and hardness while ensuring resistance to high-temperature oxidation and aqueous corrosion. Request a hypothesis for the material composition and processing method, supporting evidence on phase stability, boundary conditions for the processing temperature, and a falsification experiment to test the mechanism of property enhancement.

generation.hypothesis: Processing a lightweight AlCoCrFeNi-based multi-principal element alloy via Stationary Friction Processing (SFP) at 1800 rpm followed by a controlled aging treatment at 750 °C will simultaneously maximize hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance by stabilizing a nanocrystalline BCC/B2 matrix with a protective, Cr-rich oxide scale, while avoiding the phase separation and softening observed at higher temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) with a coarse-grained BCC/B2 microstructure and low surface free energy.
generation.intervention: Apply Stationary Friction Processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes, followed by aging at 750 °C for 20 hours.
generation.conditions: Processing performed in air; aging conducted in evacuated quartz tubes; subsequent testing in laboratory air at 850–1050 °C for 100 hours and aqueous corrosion testing.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanocrystalline grain structure (grain size reduced to ~1 μm) with high grain boundary density and a stabilized BCC/B2 phase fraction, preventing the formation of brittle ordered phases or excessive phase separation.
generation.mechanism: The high grain boundary density generated by SFP enhances diffusion paths for Cr, facilitating the rapid formation of a dense, protective Cr-rich oxide layer (chromia) during high-temperature exposure, while the subsequent aging at 750 °C (below the embrittlement regime identified in related EHEAs) suppresses excessive ordering and maintains ductility without sacrificing the hardness gained from grain refinement.
generation.predicted_outcome: The processed alloy will exhibit a hardness >400 HV, a cumulative mass gain at 850 °C reduced by >15% compared to the as-cast state, and superior aqueous corrosion resistance due to the stable, Cr-enriched surface layer, without the catastrophic failure or significant hardness loss observed at temperatures >1200 K or in molten salt environments at 650 °C.
generation.baseline: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi HEA processed without SFP, which exhibits coarse grains, lower surface free energy, and higher oxidation kinetics (0.33 mg/cm² mass gain at 850 °C).
generation.boundary: The strategy is bounded by the temperature limit of 1200 K (927 °C) for the friction process to avoid lattice disorder and melting (as seen in FeNiCrCoCu simulations), and the aging temperature must remain below 1200 °C to prevent the loss of mechanical properties observed in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 at extreme aging temperatures, though 750 °C is selected to avoid the embrittlement regime.
generation.uncertainty: While SFP at 1800 rpm increases surface free energy and oxidation resistance (PMC9026100), the specific interaction between the nanocrystalline structure and long-term aqueous corrosion resistance in this specific alloy system is not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence, and the stability of the BCC/B2 phase under prolonged high-temperature service requires verification against the phase separation risks seen in other HEAs at high temperatures.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three sets of AlCoCrFeNi samples: (1) As-cast, (2) SFP at 1800 rpm, and (3) SFP at 1800 rpm followed by aging at 750 °C. Subject all sets to cyclic oxidation at 900 °C for 200 hours and immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution for 30 days. Additionally, perform high-temperature tensile testing at 800 °C.
measurements: Oxidation kinetics (mass gain per unit area)
Surface composition analysis (XPS/EDS) to quantify Cr/Al depletion and oxide layer thickness
Microhardness (HV) and tensile strength (UTS/YS) at room and elevated temperatures
Corrosion rate (mm/year) and pitting potential in NaCl solution
Grain size and phase fraction analysis (XRD/EBSD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if: (a) the SFP+aging sample shows a mass gain increase >10% compared to the as-cast sample after oxidation, (b) the hardness drops below 300 HV after aging, or (c) the corrosion rate exceeds 5 mm/year, indicating the failure of the Cr-rich protective layer or the onset of Al/Cr depletion mechanisms similar to those observed at 650 °C in molten salt.

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a single crystal Cu matrix. Intervention: Temperature increased from 900 K to 1200 K. Processing: Molecular dynamics friction simulation; temperature controlled via Nosé–Hoover method. Test conditions: Friction simulation at 900 K and 1200 K. Structure change: Lattice disorder takes place rapidly; large number of disordered structures appeared and began to melt; dislocation density increased rapidly. Property change: Hardness decreased from 10.2 GPa to 8.6 GPa; elastic modulus decreased rapidly; wear resistance decreased sharply. Mechanism: At a temperature of 1200 K, the proportion of disordered lattice structures increases rapidly, resulting in a significant decrease in the normal force. Evidence: simulated. Quote: "At temperatures of 900 K and 1200 K, lattice disorder takes place rapidly, and dislocation density also decreases significantly, resulting in a significant decrease in the hardness and elastic modulus of the material."

Intervention effect. Base system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a single crystal Cu matrix. Intervention: Temperature increased from 900 K to 1200 K. Processing: Molecular dynamics friction simulation; temperature controlled via Nosé–Hoover method. Test conditions: Friction simulation at 900 K and 1200 K. Structure change: Lattice disorder takes place rapidly; large number of disordered structures appeared and began to melt; dislocation density increased rapidly. Property change: Hardness decreased from 10.2 GPa to 8.6 GPa; elastic modulus decreased rapidly. Mechanism: At temperatures of 900 K and 1200 K, the densities of dislocations increase rapidly resulting in a significant decrease in the hardness and elastic modulus. Evidence: simulated. Quote: "When the temperature was raised from 900 K to 1200 K, the hardness decreased slightly, from 10.2 GPa to 8.6 GPa."

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA aged at 750 °C (750A). Intervention: Aging at 1200 °C for 20 hours. Processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water. Test conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Structure change: Retention of duplex-phase microstructure with high thermal stability; some decline in fracture elongation but no catastrophic failure. Property change: UTS remains substantial at 837 MPa, YS holds at 355 MPa; fracture elongation declines but retains a notable 9.5%. Mechanism: High thermal stability of the alloy system; aging outside the embrittlement regime suppresses excessive ordering and promotes ductile interphase transition zones. Evidence: measured. Quote: "Even after aging at an extreme temperature of 1200 °C, the UTS remains substantial at 837 MPa, and the YS holds at 355 MPa."

Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Superior oxidation resistance at high temperatures due to the formation of Al- and Cr-rich oxide layers.. System: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (as-cast and composite forms).. Conditions: High temperature exposure (specifically mentioned at 1100 °C for the as-cast alloy).. Evidence: inferred. Observation: The declining oxidation rate at 1100 °C is attributed to the formation of protective Al, Cr-rich oxide layers, making the composite a promising high-temperature structural material.. Scope limits: The text cites this property for the as-cast alloy and infers it for the composite, but does not provide new high-temperature oxidation test data for the composite itself in this paper.. Alternatives: Traditional RHEAs which generally possess poor high temperature oxidation resistance.. Quote: "In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance, the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material."

Intervention effect. Base system: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Intervention: Stationary friction processing (SFP) at 400 rpm for 5 min. Processing: Stationary friction processing with a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) rotated at 400 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Structure change: Grain size refined from 98 μm to 1 μm; phase transformation from BCC/B2 to 38% FCC; microstrain increased to 0.00259; residual stress changed from +83 MPa to -90 MPa. Property change: Oxidation kinetics reduced by 12–20% compared to as-cast; cumulative mass gain at 850 °C reduced from 0.33 to 0.27 mg/cm². Mechanism: Enhanced diffusion paths due to high grain boundary density favoring formation of protective chromia. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The SFP_400 sample showed a 12–20% reduction in the oxidation kinetics"

Intervention effect. Base system: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi HEA. Intervention: Stationary friction processing (SFP) at 1800 rpm. Processing: Stationary friction processing with a WC-cylindrical tool rotated at 1800 rpm for 5 min. Test conditions: Surface free energy measurement via contact angle with water and ethanol. Structure change: Significant increase in grain boundary fraction and surface free energy. Property change: Surface free energy increased by 35.2% (from 61.75 to 83.49 mJ/m²). Mechanism: Increased reactivity of elements and favorable sites for chemisorption of O2 due to high grain boundary density. Evidence: measured. Quote: "There is a 29.8% increase in the SFE of the SFP_400 sample and a 35.2% increase in the SFE of the SFP_1800 sample"

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA). Intervention: Increase in temperature from 450 °C to 650 °C. Processing: Immersion in molten salt for 24 h at both temperatures. Test conditions: 450 °C vs 650 °C. Structure change: Cr depletion depth increased from ~30 μm to ~50 μm; Al and Cr depletion observed at both temperatures. Property change: Corrosion rate increased from ~1 mm/year to ~9 mm/year. Mechanism: Al acts as a sacrificial element; the Al/AlCl3 and Cr/CrCl2 redox couple slows dissolution of Fe, Co, and Ni. Evidence: measured. Quote: "At 450 °C, the Cr depletion depth in in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 was ~30 μm , while that for DS2205 was ~200 μm"
